items.title: The metric volume form, current flux through 3-faces and finite-chain charges
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $M$ carry an orientation in the
sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] (so that its
charts that are oriented in that orientation have orientation-preserving
transition maps), and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection. This item
fixes the metric volume form, the flux of a current through oriented $3$-faces
and finite-chain charges. The orientation of $M$ is an independent datum: it is
not determined by the metric and not by the time orientation.

**(a) Metric volume density and volume form.** Let $(U,x)$ be an oriented
chart, with metric components $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)). Define the **metric volume
density**

$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}>0\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a strictly positive smooth function because $g_{ab}$ is smooth and
$g_p$ is nondegenerate. In the chart define the local $4$-form

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}:=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3,$$

with the exterior product of [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]] and the
coordinate covector fields of
[[prop-local-coordinate-expression-for-a-differential-form]]. That these local
forms agree on chart overlaps and therefore define one smooth nowhere-vanishing
$4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — is proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (a), together
with the reading statement of clause (b) there: in every oriented chart
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^3$, and on every positively
oriented $g_p$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ one has
$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1$.

**(b) Current flux through oriented $3$-faces and chains.** Let $J$ be a
smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **current
$3$-form** of $J$ is the contraction

$$\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

the interior product of the $4$-form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ with $J$
([[def-interior-product-of-a-form-by-a-vector-field]]).

By a **smooth singular $k$-simplex** of $M$ — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-simplex` (differential-geometry track),
restated here so this page is self-contained — we mean a map
$\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ whose domain is the standard $k$-simplex
$$\Delta^k=\Bigl\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_it_i=1\Bigr\},$$
for which there exist an open set $O\subseteq A^k=\{t\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:\sum_it_i=1\}$
containing $\Delta^k$ and a smooth map $\bar\sigma:O\to M$ with
$\bar\sigma|_{\Delta^k}=\sigma$; the extension is not part of the simplex
data, and degenerate parametrizations are allowed. With the integration of
forms over such simplices
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]]), a **$3$-face** is
a smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$, and the **flux of $J$ through
$\sigma$** is the real number

$$\Phi_J(\sigma):=\int_\sigma\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

A **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** — the convention of the library
definition `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes`, restated here —
is a finite formal real linear combination $\Sigma=\sum_i c_i\sigma_i$ of
smooth singular $k$-simplices. For such a $3$-chain the **flux of $J$ through
$\Sigma$** is defined additively,

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma):=\sum_i c_i\,\Phi_J(\sigma_i),$$

a definition independent of the written expression for $\Sigma$, because a
finite formal sum is evaluated by adding the finitely many coefficients and
inserting a zero coefficient changes nothing. $\Phi_J(\Sigma)$ is the **charge**
of the current $J$ assigned to $\Sigma$ when the model reads $J$ as a conserved
current; that reading belongs to the physical postulates and is not part of
this definition.

**(c) Non-null faces and their unit normals.** A $3$-dimensional linear subspace
$H\subseteq T_pM$ is **nondegenerate** for $g_p$ when the restriction of $g_p$
to $H$ is nondegenerate, equivalently when $H\cap H^\perp=\{0\}$ in the
orthogonality of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. A
smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ is **non-null at** a parameter point $t$
when the span of the three velocity vectors
$\sigma_*\partial_1|_t,\sigma_*\partial_2|_t,\sigma_*\partial_3|_t$ has
dimension $3$ and is nondegenerate at $\sigma(t)$, and **non-null** when this holds at every
parameter point. For a non-null face the **unit normal** $\nu$ at that point is
the unique vector of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$ with $\nu\in H^\perp$,
$g(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $(\nu,\sigma_*\partial_1,\sigma_*\partial_2,
\sigma_*\partial_3)$ a positively oriented basis of $T_{\sigma(t)}M$; its
existence, uniqueness and its sign $\varepsilon:=g(\nu,\nu)$ are proved in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c), together
with the density identity of clause (c) used to read $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ on
such a face. Rank-deficient faces and rank-three faces with degenerate induced
metric are not assigned a unit normal; their flux is defined
by the $3$-form $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$ itself, as in clause (b).

items.title: Chart independence of the metric volume form, its value on orthonormal frames, and the unit normal and density of a non-null hyperplane
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) whose underlying manifold carries an
orientation ([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), and let
$w$ and the local forms $\mathrm{vol}_{g,U}$ be as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

**(a) Chart independence.** Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be oriented charts with
$x=\varphi\circ y$ on the overlap of their domains, where $\varphi$ is the
smooth transition map; write $g_{ab}$ and $g'_{ab}$ for the metric components
in the two charts and $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$,
$w'=\sqrt{|\det(g'_{ab})|}$. Then

$$\det(g'_{ab})=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)^{2}\det\bigl(g_{ab}\circ\varphi\bigr),\qquad w'=\bigl(\det D\varphi\bigr)\,(w\circ\varphi),$$

and the local forms agree on the overlap,

$$\varphi^{*}\bigl(w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\bigr)=w'\,dy^0\wedge dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3 .$$

Consequently there is a unique smooth nowhere-vanishing $4$-form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ on $M$ — the **metric volume form** — whose restriction to the
domain of every oriented chart $(U,x)$ is $w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge
dx^3$; it is a smooth section with nowhere-zero values and positive on the
given orientation.

**(b) Value on orthonormal frames.** For every $p\in M$ and every positively
oriented ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $T_pM$ with
$g_p(e_A,e_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$,

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)=1 .$$

**(c) Non-null hyperplanes: normal and density.** Let $p\in M$, let
$H\subseteq T_pM$ be a $3$-dimensional subspace that is nondegenerate for
$g_p$, and let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ be an ordered basis of $H$. Then $H^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate and $H=(H^{\perp})^{\perp}$. Let
$u\in H^{\perp}\setminus\{0\}$ and write $\nu:=u/\sqrt{|g_p(u,u)|}$, so that
$\varepsilon:=g_p(\nu,\nu)\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\delta\in\{-1,1\}$ is the sign for
which $(\delta\nu,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is a positively oriented basis of $T_pM$, then
$\nu^{*}:=\delta\nu$ is the **unit normal to $H$ adapted to the ordered basis**
$(v_1,v_2,v_3)$; it satisfies $g_p(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})=\varepsilon$,
$g_p(\nu^{*},h)=0$ for every $h\in H$, and it is the unique vector with these
two properties for which $(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)$ is positively oriented.
Moreover

$$\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(\nu^{*},v_1,v_2,v_3)=\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_p(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|}.$$

items.title: The derivative of the metric density and the chart formula for the divergence of a vector field
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and let $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ be the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a) on $U$. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

items.title: Divergence, Stokes flux balance and the non-null face formula for a Lorentzian current
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

items.title: Lorentzian metrics are stable under small compactly supported symmetric perturbations
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), so that at every $p\in M$ the form
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$, and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) whose
support is compact.

**(a) Pointwise openness.** Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $4$
and let $G$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ of inertia $(3,1,0)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). If in some basis of $V$ the matrix of $G$
has the form $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E$, then $G$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$
whenever $|E_{ij}|<1/8$ for all $i,j$. Consequently, for every basis the set
of matrices of symmetric forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$ is open in the space
$M_4^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with respect to the maximum-entry norm, and
equivalently $g_p$ has a neighborhood in the space of symmetric forms at $p$
consisting entirely of forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$.

**(b) Global stability.** There is $\lambda_0>0$ such that for every real
$\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the smooth symmetric field $g+\lambda h$
is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with
time orientation inherited from $N$ (the field $N$ remains timelike for
$g+\lambda h$ for $|\lambda|$ small).

items.title: A continuous symmetric coefficient orthogonal to every compactly supported variation vanishes
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ with inverse metric $g^{-1}$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), let $(U,x)$ be a smooth
chart, let $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ be the metric density on $U$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a)), and let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

items.title: The Hilbert stress-energy tensor of a metric-dependent action
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating an oriented top-form density and the action for the reversed
orientation is defined by that same integral convention, reversing orientation
changes both the action variation and the volume-form integral by a sign,
leaving the tensor in the defining identity unchanged.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Hilbert stress-energy tensor
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold,
let $c>0$, let $S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ and $\varphi$ be as in
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]; in particular, $\mathcal D$ admits
every compactly supported metric direction at $(g,\varphi)$. Suppose that $T$
and $T'$ are both Hilbert stress-energy tensors of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with
respect to $c$ relative to the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then $T=T'$ on $M$; hence the
definite article in "the Hilbert stress-energy tensor" is justified.

items.title: First variation of the Einstein-Hilbert density under compactly supported metric variations, and of the timelike length functional
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

items.title: Killing fields of a Lorentzian metric
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

items.title: Killing fields and conserved currents, and on-shell conservation of the Hilbert stress-energy tensor
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

items.title: The scalar-field matter model of the classical gravitational framework
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

items.title: First variation, Hilbert tensor and conservation of the scalar-field model
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions with $\varphi_{u=0}=\varphi$ such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar equation at each point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and therefore everywhere if that set is dense, by continuity. No converse follows on an open constant-field region.

items.title: The dust matter model: rest density, four-velocity, stress-energy and dust system
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The parameter $\rho$ is the coefficient in the unit-normalized tensor of
clause (b); this mathematical definition assigns it no physical unit. In the
framework's SI stress-energy reading it is the **rest energy density**
$\varepsilon:=\rho$, in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The **rest-mass
density** is instead $\rho_m:=\varepsilon/c^2$, in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the physical four-velocity is
$U:=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Thus the same tensor is
$T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b=\rho_m U^aU^b$. A purely mathematical or
$c=1$ convention may rescale the density coefficient; interpreting $\rho$
as an SI mass density while keeping the unit tangent $u$ would require the
explicit tensor $c^2\rho\,u\otimes u$. Physical realizations and readings
are adopted by the matter postulate, not deduced here.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

items.title: The perfect-fluid matter model: rest energy density, pressure, four-velocity and stress-energy
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

items.title: Divergence-free dust is exactly the dust system, and divergence-free perfect fluid is exactly the fluid equations
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

items.title: Adopted classical gravitational action and variational field law
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, for
models whose geometric data satisfy [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]
and whose matter sector satisfies [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the
following statements. All symbols $c,G_N,\Lambda,\kappa$ are those of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(i) Oriented models.** The spacetime of a model in this formulation carries,
in addition to $(M,g,N)$, an orientation
([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]); the metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and its
integrals are understood with respect to it. A model without a chosen
orientation, or with a nonorientable $M$, requires the density formulation of
the action, which is not developed here and is outside the scope of this
postulate.

**(ii) Einstein-Hilbert action density.** The **Einstein-Hilbert action
density** of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ is
the smooth $4$-form

$$\ell_{\mathrm{EH}}(g'):=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\bigl(S_{g'}-2\Lambda\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_{g'},$$

where $S_{g'}$ is the scalar curvature of $g'$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]) and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ is
a constant parameter of dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. For two metrics whose
difference is supported in a compact set, the **action difference**
$\Delta S_{\mathrm{EH}}:=\int_M[\ell_{\mathrm{EH}}(g')-\ell_{\mathrm{EH}}(g)]$
is a real number. Only such differences are used; no value of the total action
of a noncompact spacetime is asserted. The coupling

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}$$

has dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{2}$.

**(iii) Matter sectors and available presentations.** A model adopting this
action presentation uses the supplied scalar-field action in sector (1).
Sectors (2) and (3) are described here only to distinguish the alternative
direct-equation presentation; they do not adopt this variational postulate.
The three sector descriptions use the units of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]:

1. a **scalar-field sector**, specified by the data $(\varphi,V,K)$ of
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with the physical readings: $\varphi$
   dimensionless, $V$ a geometric potential with values in
   $\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $K>0$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}$. Length
   coordinates give $\partial_a\varphi$ dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, so the
   kinetic term and $V$ have matching dimensions; the physical potential
   energy density is $K V$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The sector's
   action differences are those defined there, and its stress-energy tensor
   is the candidate tensor of that definition;
2. a **dust sector**, specified by $(\rho,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]], whose unit-tangent coefficient is the rest
   energy density $\varepsilon:=\rho$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; the
   rest-mass density is $\rho_m=\varepsilon/c^2$ in
   $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the physical four-velocity is $U=cu$
   with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Its stress-energy tensor
   $T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b=\rho_m U^aU^b$ is prescribed by the model
   and its matter equations are the dust system of that definition;
3. a **perfect-fluid sector**, specified by $(\varepsilon,p,n)$ (with optional
   equation of state) of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with
   $\varepsilon,p$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, whose stress-energy tensor
   is prescribed by the model and whose matter equations are the fluid
   equations of that definition.

In sectors (2) and (3) no matter action is supplied: the model prescribes
$T$ and the matter equations directly and adopts the direct-equation
presentation, with its consistency conditions. Clause (iv) does not apply to
these sectors. In
sector (1) the matter action is the scalar action of
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]; its metric variation is required to be
represented by its stress-energy tensor in the Hilbert convention

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}\,\delta g^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g \qquad\text{off shell in matter variables,}$$

which is the content of
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]] clause (b) for that action; for the
scalar action this representation is a proved property of the model, recorded
in [[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]] clause (b), and is
adopted here as the reading of $T$ in the framework's units.

**(iv) Variational field law.** For the supplied scalar-field action, the classical field
law adopted for the model is: the metric $g$ is stationary for the total action
difference $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\Delta S_{\mathrm{EH}}+\Delta S_m$ under
every jointly smooth metric family with compactly supported variation as
defined in [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]] clause (a), and the model's matter configuration satisfies its matter equations
of motion. This variational principle is the adopted field law of the action
presentation; the displayed field equation it is equivalent to is derived, not
adopted a second time, in
[[pthm-gr-adopted-action-and-einstein-equations]].

**(v) Alternative presentation.** The direct-equation presentation of the same
field law is adopted separately in
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]. A model adopts exactly one of the two
presentations; they are alternative presentations of one classical field law
and are never combined as two independent premises.

**(vi) Status and scope.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions. No
geometry, symmetry principle or observation derives them; the action
formulation is not claimed to be selected by nature, and no numerical value of
$c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply verbatim: lower-dimensional or
distributional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields require mathematics and physical assumptions not supplied here, and the
comparison of any model prediction with data tests the combined model,
including this postulate, rather than proving it.

items.physical_scope: Adoption of the action formulation of the classical gravitational field law: the Einstein-Hilbert action of the smooth Lorentzian metric with cosmological parameter Lambda, the supplied scalar-field matter action (dust and perfect-fluid sectors use the separate direct-equation presentation), the Hilbert convention for the matter stress-energy tensor, and the variational principle as the field law of the model. Excludes quantum gravity and quantum fields, non-smooth and distributional sources, boundaries and junction conditions, gravity-mediated matter self-force corrections, and any claim that an action principle or a particular matter model describes nature. The adopted fields, constants and equations are model input; deductions from them are conditional on this adoption.

items.title: Adopted Einstein field equation in the direct-equation presentation
items.statement:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

items.title: Stationarity of the adopted total action is equivalent to the Einstein equation with the framework's coupling
items.statement:
Adopt the action formulation of the framework, that is, the action density and
matter sectors of [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]], for a model whose
geometric data and matter sector satisfy
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]; let $(M,g,N)$ be oriented with metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]],
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and suppose the
model's matter sector supplies a stress-energy tensor field $T$ on $M$
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]])
which is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the matter action at $(g,\varphi)$
with respect to $c$ ([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]); in particular
this holds in the scalar-field sector, where the model is
$(\varphi,V,K)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] and the claim is
supplied by [[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]] clause (b).

**(a) Equivalence.** With $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ the Einstein tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), the following are
equivalent:

1. the metric $g$ is stationary for the total action difference
   $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S_{\mathrm{EH}}+\Delta S_m$ under every
   smooth family of smooth Lorentzian metrics $s\mapsto g_s$ with $g_0=g$ and
   compactly supported variation;
2. $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ at every point of $M$.

**(b) The two presentations agree.** Consequently, in the action presentation
the classical field law of clause (iv) of
[[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]] has the same equation form
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ as the field law adopted in the
direct-equation presentation [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]; the two
presentations are equivalent descriptions of one classical field law, and a
model adopts exactly one of them. In the prescribed-$T$ sectors (dust and
perfect fluid) the equation is adopted directly, as recorded in clause (iii)
of [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]], and its consistency condition
is derived separately on this page.

items.title: Consistency conditions of the adopted field law: conservation, trace, parameter variation and the energy conditions of a perfect fluid
items.statement:
Adopt one of the two presentations of the framework's field law, that is,
[[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]] or
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]], for a model with geometric data and matter
sector satisfying [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
and curvature tensors $R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$,
$G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let $T$ be the model's smooth
symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the matter domain
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]), let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the
constant parameter and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ as in
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be the
model's open matter domain and suppose the field law holds on $U$,

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U .$$

**(a) Necessary conservation.** $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Consequently a
prescribed smooth symmetric $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}\neq0$ at some point cannot
satisfy the field law there with that proposed metric; the divergence is
computed using its metric-selected connection, and may change if the metric
is changed.

**(b) Trace.** On $U$, $g^{ab}T_{ab}$ satisfies
$-S+4\Lambda=\kappa\,g^{ab}T_{ab}$.

**(c) Parameter variation.** If instead $\Lambda:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth
function and the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds on $U$
with that function in place of a constant, then on $U$

$$\kappa\nabla^aT_{ab}=\partial_b\Lambda .$$

Consequently, at every point where $d\Lambda\ne0$, the equation requires
$\nabla^aT_{ab}\ne0$; where $d\Lambda=0$, this identity imposes conservation.
A smooth $\Lambda$ can be locally constant but nonconstant across disconnected
components of $U$, in which case this identity does not force nonconservation.

**(d) A vacuum solution.** In the global vacuum example take
$U=M=\mathbb R^4$ with the identity chart and the flat metric
$g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ (a smooth Lorentzian metric
with time orientation $N=\partial_0$), the field law with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$
holds: $G=0$ and $S=0$ for the flat metric. With $T=0$ and $\Lambda\neq0$ it
fails, since $G+\Lambda g=\Lambda g\neq0$.

**(e) Energy conditions are additional assumptions.** Neither adopted
presentation of the field law contains a clause imposing any of the weak, null,
dominant or strong energy conditions of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]]; none of
the four is a universal consequence of that equation, as the direct-equation
perfect-fluid model in the proof shows. Particular matter models may imply
energy conditions; when not derived, they are additional assumptions in the
sense of clause (iv) of [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]].

**(f) Perfect-fluid rest-frame reading.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a
perfect-fluid model on its matter domain
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]), and at any $p\in U$ let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n_p$. Then
$T_{AB}=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,p,p,p)$ in that basis, and at $p$

$$T\ \text{satisfies WEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies NEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+p\ge0,\qquad T\ \text{satisfies DEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge|p|,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies SEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+3p\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0 .$$

In particular a model with $\varepsilon>0$ and $p=-\varepsilon$ satisfies the
NEC, WEC and DEC and violates the SEC; the inequality signs here are those of
the strict-timelike convention of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]], under which
continuity extensions to the causal cone are not assumed.

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 3.4.1 and 4.5.7: the contracted Bianchi identity (3.40)-(3.44) and the energy conditions with the perfect-fluid and cosmological specializations, printed pp. 130-134 and 194-198 (PDF pp. 137-141 and 201-205)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 (3.94), printed p. 82 (PDF p. 89), and Ch. 4: the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) with the perfect-fluid reading, printed p. 118 (PDF p. 125)

items.physical_scope: Smooth classical domain of the framework in either presentation of the adopted field law: an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, a constant cosmological parameter, a smooth stress-energy tensor on the model's matter domain, and the field equation G_{ab}+Lambda g_{ab}=kappa T_{ab}. The conclusions are conditional consequences of the adopted field law; they assert no existence, no propagation and no empirical fact, and none of the four energy conditions is universally forced by the field equation; particular matter models may imply some, and otherwise they are additional assumptions.

items.title: Scope and conventions of the Einstein-and-matter page: presentations, matter sectors and open obligations
items.statement:
## Scope, status and conventions

This note fixes the scope of the page's field-law and matter content and the
status of its claims; it proves nothing by itself.

- **Two presentations, one field law.** The framework adopts the classical
  field law in exactly one of two presentations for any given model: the
  action formulation [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]] or the
  direct-equation formulation [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]. The theorem
  [[pthm-gr-adopted-action-and-einstein-equations]] identifies the equation
  form of the two presentations, so they define one classical field law rather
  than two independent premises; a model never adopts both.

- **Adopted versus derived.** The field law, the matter sectors, the
  cosmological parameter and the Hilbert convention are adopted model input.
  The equation form of the action presentation, the conservation and trace
  identities, the parameter-variation identity and the rest-frame readings of
  the energy conditions are conditional deductions recorded in
  [[pthm-gr-adopted-action-and-einstein-equations]] and
  [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]]. None of the adopted
  statements is derived from mathematics, symmetry or observation, and none of
  the deductions asserts that the model describes nature.

- **Matter sectors.** The matter content is one of the sectors of clause (iii)
  of [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]: the scalar-field model with a
  supplied action and Hilbert tensor in the action presentation, or the dust
  and perfect-fluid models with prescribed stress-energy tensor and matter
  equations in the direct-equation presentation. The stress-energy
  tensor occupies the slot defined in [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]];
  its component reading in a $g$-orthonormal frame is in
  $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the coupling satisfies
  $\kappa T\sim\mathrm m^{-2}$ with $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ in the conventions of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The equation of state of a
  fluid sector is a further assumption of that model; the energy conditions of
  [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] are optional additional assumptions unless a particular matter model
  implies them; the field equation alone does not universally force them.

- **Smooth oriented branch.** The material assumes the smooth-branch
  restriction of [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
  [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] and, for the action and flux
  constructions, an orientation of the model's spacetime. Distributional or
  lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, low-regularity
  fields and quantum matter lie outside this page; they require further
  mathematics and, where physical, further adopted assumptions.

- **Empirical status.** The page contains no experiment, no measured input and
  no empirical premise. Predictions computed from a fully specified model —
  geometry, matter sector and field law — may later be compared with reported
  observations; such a comparison tests the combined model and its auxiliary
  assumptions, and agreement is evidence rather than a proof of any postulate.

- **Deferred obligations.** The broader observer-dependent energy-current
  discussion and the limits on global gravitational energy are treated on the
  local-and-global energy page; this page already proves the divergence and
  finite-chain flux balance for smooth currents, including Killing currents.
  The flat and Newtonian limits, the spherical vacuum, the
  homogeneous cosmologies and the linearized wave models are treated on their
  own pages. This page states no existence, uniqueness or propagation theorem
  for solutions of the field equation, and no initial-value or global causal
  claim.

items.title: Metric density, volume form and current flux of the flat metric in the identity chart
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the flat
Lorentzian metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the time orientation
$N=\partial_0$ and the orientation for which the identity chart is oriented
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]); let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection of $g$ and $\mathrm{vol}_g$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). Then:

1. The metric density and the volume form are $w=1$ and
   $\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ in the identity
   chart, and $\mathrm{vol}_g(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)=1$.
2. The connection is the coordinate connection, $\Gamma\equiv0$, so that
   $\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a$ for every smooth vector field $J$ and the
   divergence formula $w^{-1}\partial_a(wJ^a)$ reduces to the coordinate
   divergence.
3. For $J=x^1\partial_1$ the divergence is $\nabla_aJ^a=1$, the current form is
   $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g=-x^1\,dx^0\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and
   $d(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)=\mathrm{vol}_g$, in accordance with
   [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (a).
4. Let $\Delta^3=\{(t_1,t_2,t_3):t_i\ge0,\ t_1+t_2+t_3\le1\}$ with its
   coordinate orientation and coordinate volume $1/6$. The affine simplex
   $\sigma_-(t)=(t_1,0,t_2,t_3)$ has adapted normal $-\partial_1$, so the flux
   of $J=\partial_1$ through it is $-1/6$. The affine simplex
   $\sigma_+(t)=(t_2,a,t_1,t_3)$ on the parallel plane $x^1=a$ has adapted
   normal $+\partial_1$, so its flux is $+1/6$. Both induced metric densities
   on the parameter simplex equal $1$; the signs follow from the stated
   parameter orientations and the ambient chart orientation.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 8.6-8.7: the volume element and Stokes' theorem in a chart, printed pp. 108-110 (PDF pp. 109-111)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2 'tensor densities' (2.44) and the integration measure sqrt|g|, printed pp. 52-54 (PDF pp. 59-61)

items.title: A divergence-free current with nonzero face-flux density: J=x^1∂_2 in flat space
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the time orientation $N=\partial_0$ and the
chart orientation, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]],
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). Let

$$J:=x^1\partial_2$$

be the smooth vector field of [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]].
Then:

1. $\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_2x^1=0$: the current is divergence-free.
2. The current $3$-form is
   $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g=x^1\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^3$, and
   $d(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$ identically, consistently with clause (a) of
   [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]].
3. The pointwise flux density of $J$ through a non-null face with adapted unit
   normal $\nu^{*}$ is $\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\sqrt{|\det(g(v_i,v_j))|}$; for
   the coordinate directions this is
   $$0\ \text{for }\nu^{*}=\pm\partial_0,\pm\partial_1,\qquad x^1\ \text{for }\nu^{*}=\partial_2,\qquad -x^1\ \text{for }\nu^{*}=-\partial_2 .$$
   Thus the divergence-free current has nonzero flux density through the faces
   normal to $\partial_2$: vanishing divergence does not mean vanishing flux
   through every face, and the flux balance
   $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$ of clause (b) of
   [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] controls the side
   boundary genuinely.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5 with figures 40-41: the charge balance with the timelike boundary B and the requirement of vanishing flux through B, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 8.7: Stokes' theorem with the side boundary, printed pp. 109-110 (PDF pp. 110-111)

items.title: Dust in flat space: a conserved homogeneous model and a nonconserved time-dependent density
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation $N=\partial_0$, with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$; let $u:=\partial_0$, a smooth
future-directed unit timelike vector field on $M=\mathbb R^4$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Then:

1. For every smooth $\rho:\mathbb R^4\to(0,\infty)$ with $\partial_0\rho=0$,
   the pair $(\rho,u)$ is a dust model on $M$ whose dust system holds and whose
   stress-energy tensor is divergence-free.
2. On the open subset $U:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:x^0>-1\}$ the pair
   $(\rho|_U,u|_U)$ with $\rho(t,x)=1+t$ is a dust model on $U$ whose dust
   system fails and whose stress-energy tensor has
   $\nabla^aT_{ab}=-\delta^0{}_b\neq0$ on $U$.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 (1.104)-(1.113): the energy-momentum tensor of dust and its conservation, printed pp. 28-31 (PDF pp. 35-38)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.2: the pressureless case and the geodesic motion of the fluid particles, printed pp. 65-66 (PDF pp. 66-67)

items.title: A scalar field with null-or-zero gradient in flat space: equation of motion and conservation
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the chart orientation, with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]). Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$
be a smooth function, let

$$\varphi(x):=f(x^0+x^1),$$

and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model with $V\equiv0$ and
$K>0$ ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]). Then:

1. $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=0$: the metric dual of $d\varphi$ is
   null wherever $d\varphi\ne0$ and is zero wherever $d\varphi=0$.
2. $\Box_g\varphi=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi=0$: $\varphi$ satisfies the scalar
   equation of motion, and its stress-energy tensor is
   $T_{ab}=K\,\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi$.
3. $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$: the tensor is divergence-free, and $T(v,v)=K(\partial_a\varphi\,v^a)^2\ge0$
   for every $v\in T_pM$, with equality exactly on the kernel $\partial_a\varphi\,v^a=0$; this is a hyperplane where $d\varphi\ne0$ and the full tangent space where $d\varphi=0$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 9.1 and 9.3: the wave equation for a free scalar field and its energy-momentum tensor (9.31)-(9.32), printed pp. 111-116 (PDF pp. 112-117)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 4.5.1 and 4.5.3: the free scalar field equation and its energy-momentum tensor (4.51), printed pp. 180-185 (PDF pp. 187-192)

items.title: The Killing current of a static dust congruence in flat space
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart, the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the time orientation $N=\partial_0$ and the
chart orientation, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $\xi:=\partial_0$, let
$\rho:\mathbb R^4\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth with $\partial_0\rho=0$, and let
$u:=\partial_0$, so that $(\rho,u)$ is a dust model on $M$ with tensor
$T^{ab}=\rho u^au^b$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then:

1. $\xi=\partial_0$ is a Killing field.
2. The current $J^a:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ equals $J=-\rho\,u$, and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$.
3. $\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g=-\rho\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$: the current
   $3$-form is (minus) the rest density carried by the constant-$x^0$ slices,
   and its flux through corresponding regions of two slices is equal because
   $\partial_0\rho=0$.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 5.3: Killing vectors and the conserved quantity X_a V^a along geodesics, printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42): Killing vectors and conserved quantities along geodesics, printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149)

items.title: The weak energy condition does not imply conservation of a prescribed stress-energy tensor
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the identity chart, and let $U$ be an
open subset. Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
which satisfies the weak energy condition of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]]:
$T_p(v,v)\ge0$ for every timelike $v\in T_pM$ and every $p\in U$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Then $T$ is conserved,
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$."

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) and the statement that conservation of T_{mu nu} is not implied by pointwise positivity, printed p. 118 (PDF p. 125)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.7: the energy conditions are assumptions on T, distinct from its conservation, printed pp. 194-198 (PDF pp. 201-205)

items.physical_scope: Pointwise algebraic statement about a prescribed smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor field on an open region of the flat classical spacetime model: the weak energy condition is a pointwise positivity condition on the tensor and carries no conservation content. No dynamical model, no solution of the field equation, no measurement and no claim about nature is asserted; the example shows only that the named condition is not by itself the conservation identity.

items.title: A divergence-free current with nonzero flux through a timelike 3-simplex
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the identity chart and the chart
orientation, and let $J$ be a smooth vector field on $M$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $M$ ([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Then the flux
$\Phi_J(\sigma)$ of $J$ through every smooth singular $3$-simplex $\sigma$ of
$M$ vanishes."

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 8.7: Stokes' theorem in the form flux equality up to the side boundary, printed pp. 109-110 (PDF pp. 110-111)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.5: the charge through a spatial slice and the role of the boundary flux, printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196)

items.title: Energy-condition verdicts for dust, radiation and the cosmological effective fluid
items.statement:
Adopt a perfect-fluid model $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ in the classical framework
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]) and use the rest-frame equivalences of
[[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]] clause (f): at a point
with rest frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $e_0=n$, the four conditions of
[[def-gr-energy-conditions]] read

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff\varepsilon\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0,\qquad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\varepsilon+p\ge0,\qquad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\varepsilon\ge|p|,\qquad \mathrm{SEC}\iff\varepsilon+3p\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0 .$$

Then:

1. **Dust** ($p=0$, $\varepsilon>0$): WEC, NEC, DEC and SEC all hold.
2. **Radiation** ($p=\varepsilon/3$, $\varepsilon>0$): WEC, NEC, DEC and SEC all
   hold.
3. **Positive cosmological effective fluid** ($\varepsilon>0$,
   $p=-\varepsilon$, as for the term $-\Lambda g_{ab}/\kappa$ with
   $\Lambda>0$ in [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]): WEC, NEC and DEC hold (with
   equality in the non-strict inequalities) and SEC fails.
4. **Negative cosmological effective fluid** ($\varepsilon<0$,
   $p=-\varepsilon$, $\Lambda<0$): WEC and DEC fail, NEC holds with equality
   and SEC holds. Together with clause 3, this shows that WEC and SEC are
   incomparable by implication.

references.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.7: the perfect-fluid energy conditions and the cosmological-constant case, printed pp. 194-198 (PDF pp. 201-205)
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 4: the Weak Energy Condition and the perfect-fluid specialization, printed pp. 117-118 (PDF pp. 124-125)

items.physical_scope: Pointwise algebraic reading of the four energy conditions for prescribed perfect-fluid models in a rest frame, including the effective fluid associated with a cosmological parameter in the adopted field law. No dynamics, no solution of any field equation, no measurement and no claim about nature is asserted; the example records the inequalities alone.
